pr_body:
When this option is true, the service restarts without entering a failed state. Dependent units are not notified of transitory failure.
    
This is useful for the following use case:
    

> We have a target with `Requires=my-service`, `After=my-service`. `my-service.service` is a oneshot service and has `Restart=on-failure` in its definition.
> 
> `my-service` can get stuck for various reasons and time out, in which case it is restarted. Currently, when it fails the first time, the target fails, even though `my-service` is restarted.
> 
> The behavior we're looking for is that until `my-service` is not restarted anymore, the target stays pending waiting for `my-service` to start successfully or fail without being restarted anymore.

Closes #20412.

This is the followup of this PR: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/26751

In some cases, we don't want a dependent unit to fail if a dependency fails **temporarily**, i.e. fails at first but succeeds after restart. The use case is described in PR: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/26751:

issue_context.title: Service enters "failed" state even if it is restarted
issue_context.body:
I would like to distinguish between failed services that will be restarted from ones that will not be restarted anymore.

Currently, when active service fails it enters "failed" state before entering "activating" again due to Restart= entry in the service file. This makes it hard to determine whether the service has failed but will be restarted or it has failed and will not be restarted.

I was reading the following documentation and it suggests that service enters “failed” state only after it can’t be restarted anymore:
https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.service.html
> Note that service restart is subject to unit start rate limiting configured with StartLimitIntervalSec= and StartLimitBurst=, see systemd.unit(5) for details. **A restarted service enters the failed state only after the start limits are reached.**

Either it's a bug or the sentence is not precise. This is an example of a service that fails three times before it stops being restarted due to StartLimitBurst=. State changes were reported through dbus org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.PropertiesChanged signal on Unit.

```
test.service:
[Unit]
StartLimitIntervalSec=10
StartLimitBurst=3

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=bash -c "sleep 1; exit 1"
Restart=on-failure
```
```
busctl monitor --system org.freedesktop.systemd1
systemctl start test.service
```
```
ActiveState   SubState
--------------------------
inactive      dead
active        running
failed        failed
activating    auto-restart
inactive      dead
active        running
failed        failed
activating    auto-restart
inactive      dead
active        running
failed        failed
activating    auto-restart
inactive      dead
failed        failed
```
As you can see it enters failed state multiple times so it's not possible to know which one is final.

Suggestions:
1) Don't enter "failed" state if the service will be restarted, the service can still recover so it has not failed yet. Go from active straight to activating:
```
ActiveState   SubState
--------------------------
active        running
(failure)
activating    auto-restart
```

2) Enter "inactive" state instead of "failed" if the service will be restarted
```
ActiveState   SubState
--------------------------
active        running
inactive      dead
activating    auto-restart
```

3) Specify in substate that the service will be restarted, for example:
```
ActiveState   SubState
--------------------------
active        running
failed        will-restart
activating    auto-restart
```

`systemd 247 (247.3-6)`
